overall: The meeting looks mostly regular, with a clear agenda, a Zoom link and a recorded chair announcement; there was no executive session. The open questions are the agenda file being created under 48 counted hours ahead, a possible remote member with voice votes, the broad item 5a, and gaps in the minutes.

findings.title: Agenda file made 47 counted hours before the meeting
findings.summary: This agenda file was made 46.9 counted hours before the meeting, so this version could not have been posted 48 hours ahead. The file’s clock carries no timezone; Eastern time is assumed. Read as UTC it would be four hours earlier.

rule.quote: a public body shall post notice of every meeting at least 48 hours prior to the meeting, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and legal holidays
rule.label: G.L. c.30A §20 (malegislature.gov)

evidence.note: the PDF’s own creation time, read by scripts/extract_document_timestamps.py; the earliest this file could have been posted

findings.settle: The clerk’s posting record for this notice (the time it went up on the board and the website), and any earlier version.

findings.title: The posted agenda shows no posting date or time
findings.status: cannot tell from what is published
findings.summary: The agenda text carries the meeting date, time, place and a Zoom link. It does not show when it was posted, and does not say whether it was revised.

rule.quote: The date and time that a meeting notice is posted shall be conspicuously recorded thereon or therewith.
rule.label: 940 CMR 29.00, Open Meeting Law regulations (Attorney General, clean version)

evidence.quote: Broadcast Status: HYBRID MEETING (in person and on Zoom)

findings.settle: The notice as it appeared on the official posting site, or the clerk's date-and-time stamp.

findings.title: A voice vote was taken, and a remote participant may have been a member
findings.summary: The captions have the chair welcoming someone on Zoom ('Cara') at the start, and the vote on Scenario 2 was a voice vote ('all in favor?'). The minutes give the count 3-0-1 without names and name no member as remote. The record does not show whether a member was remote, which would have required a roll call.

rule.quote: All votes taken during any meeting in which a member participates remotely shall be by roll call vote.
rule.label: 940 CMR 29.00, Open Meeting Law regulations (Attorney General, clean version)

findings.title: Agenda item 5a is broad for what was discussed and voted
findings.summary: The agenda lists one action item, 'Additional Funding for Education'. The committee voted on a three-scenario spending plan and on a motion backing citizen-petition Article 3 at Special Town Meeting. The agenda names neither the scenarios nor the warrant articles, though the committee may have thought these were covered.

rule.quote: The list of topics shall have sufficient specificity to reasonably advise the public of the issues to be discussed at the meeting.
rule.label: 940 CMR 29.00, Open Meeting Law regulations (Attorney General, clean version)

evidence.quote: The Committee then reviewed Article 3, a citizen petition seeking $151,338.38 from certified free cash

findings.settle: Any supporting materials posted with the agenda (the slides or packet) and whether the notice linked them.

findings.title: Refund of a transportation donation was not an agenda item
findings.summary: The committee discussed, and the captions have the chair stating, that a transportation donation already accepted would be refunded to the boosters. No agenda item names gifts or donations. The record does not show why it came up.

rule.quote: a listing of topics that the chair reasonably anticipates will be discussed at the meeting.

findings.settle: The earlier minutes accepting the donation, and whether the chair anticipated the topic 48 hours ahead.

findings.title: Votes are recorded with outcomes, but without who voted how
findings.summary: The minutes record the Scenario 2 motion (mover, seconder, 3-0-1), the Article 3 support motion and the adjournment, all in open session. The Article 3 and adjournment motions have no named mover or seconder.

rule.quote: the decisions made and the actions taken at each meeting, including the record of all votes.
rule.label: G.L. c.30A §22 (malegislature.gov)

evidence.quote: The motion passed, 3-0-1, with Ms. Young abstaining.

findings.settle: The approved minutes, or a roll-call record, if one exists.

rule.quote: Minutes of all open and executive sessions shall be created and approved in a timely manner.
rule.label: 940 CMR 29.00, Open Meeting Law regulations (Attorney General, clean version)

findings.settle: The agenda or minutes of the next School Committee meetings, showing an approval vote.

cannot_see: Deliberation outside a meeting — emails, texts or conversations among a quorum of members — leaves no trace in an agenda, minutes or a recording.
When the notice was actually posted, and where. We hold the agenda file and the moment that file was made; the clerk’s posting time is not in anything published here.
Anything in documents used at the meeting but not posted (handouts, slides, the executive session minutes themselves).
Whether executive session minutes exist, and whether they were reviewed for release as the law requires.
Anything said off-microphone, or before the recording started and after it stopped.
